records.summary: The property at 243 West Portal Ave is in the West Portal NCD zoning district, where a restaurant on the first story is principally permitted without a conditional use authorization. The site history shows two 2012 Planning approvals for restaurant use with a Type 41 ABC license (beer and wine), indicating this address has operated as a restaurant. The immediate vicinity is densely developed with food and drink businesses: 11 registered businesses within 500 ft, including one bar, and 4 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 ft (Types 41, 42, and 48). Within 1,000 ft over the last 10 years, only 4 dated use decisions are on record for food/drink concepts, all approved (3 outright, 1 with conditions), with no denials—though the sample is too small to compute a statistically meaningful approval rate.

comparables.why_comparable: This is the subject property itself (243-255 West Portal Ave, 0 m away). An agency referral in 2012 approved a Type 41 ABC license (beer and wine) for a restaurant use at the exact address the concept proposes to occupy.
comparables.key_takeaway: The site has prior approval for restaurant use with beer and wine service, confirming that the NCD-WEST PORTAL zoning permits restaurant operations at this address and that the address can support food service infrastructure.

comparables.why_comparable: Also the subject property (243-255 West Portal Ave, 0 m), filed three months after MB1200147 in 2012. This agency referral approved continuation of an existing nonconforming restaurant use under Planning Code Section 186.1 after the code was amended.
comparables.key_takeaway: The property operated as a restaurant in 2012 and Planning approved its continuation as a nonconforming use, indicating flexibility for restaurant uses at this site even when code changes occurred. The current concept as a principally permitted use faces fewer barriers.

comparables.why_comparable: A 2019 CUA for Kaleifornia restaurant at 36 West Portal Ave (285 m away, same NCD-WEST PORTAL district). This was a use decision requiring a Planning Commission hearing for a new restaurant, approved with conditions including restrictive hours.
comparables.key_takeaway: The one recent conditioned approval in the neighborhood imposed strict operating hours of 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily, plus standard eating-and-drinking conditions (trash, noise, odor control, community liaison). This suggests the Commission may condition even non-alcohol restaurant operations if evening activity is proposed, though the current concept's pre-midnight hours are less sensitive.

comparables.why_comparable: A 2015 CUA at 160 West Portal Ave (109 m away, NCD-WEST PORTAL) approving a change from Limited Restaurant to full Restaurant for Toast Eatery. This is a use decision showing an intensification of food use on the same block.
comparables.key_takeaway: Approval to expand from limited to full restaurant service at a nearby address confirms the district supports full-service dining. The absence of extracted conditions suggests a straightforward approval when the use is principally permitted and well-operated.

comparables.why_comparable: A 2011 CUA at 170 West Portal Ave (109 m away, NCD-WEST PORTAL) approving a change of use to full-service restaurant (Sweet Orchid). This is a use decision from the Planning Commission for a new full-service restaurant in the same district.
comparables.key_takeaway: Full-service restaurant approved without extracted conditions in the immediate West Portal corridor, reinforcing that the neighborhood supports dining establishments when they comply with zoning and operational standards.

comparables.why_comparable: A 2020 agency referral at 118 West Portal Ave (148 m away, NCD-WEST PORTAL) for a Limited Restaurant (Shaw's) involving a change of ownership and continuation of existing use. This is an agency referral, not a Commission decision, so it carries less weight but shows recent activity.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning routinely approves continuation and ownership changes for existing restaurant uses via the referral process, demonstrating that restaurant operations are well-established and accepted in the district.

comparables.why_comparable: A 2015 agency referral at 301 West Portal Ave (97 m away, NCD-WEST PORTAL) for Fuji Restaurant, documenting continuation of an existing restaurant with ABC license that had operated since 1999, with hours until 10:30 p.m. This is an agency referral showing long-standing restaurant operations.
comparables.key_takeaway: A restaurant with evening hours (closing at 10:30 p.m. weekdays, 10 p.m. weekends) has operated successfully at a nearby address since 1999, indicating the neighborhood tolerates restaurant activity into the evening, well beyond the 8 p.m. limit imposed on Kaleifornia.

comparables.why_comparable: A 2015 CUA at 44-50 West Portal Ave (274 m away, NCD-WEST PORTAL) approving a Formula Retail Limited Restaurant (Quickly bubble tea chain). This is a use decision for formula retail, which typically faces neighborhood resistance, yet it was approved.
comparables.key_takeaway: Even a formula retail restaurant requiring extra scrutiny under Planning Code Section 303 was approved in West Portal, suggesting the Commission prioritizes appropriate operations over brand identity. A non-formula independent restaurant faces fewer hurdles.

comparables.why_comparable: A 1991 CUA at 260 West Portal Ave (68 m away, NCD-WEST PORTAL) converting a wine shop into a full-service restaurant. This is an older use decision but demonstrates long-standing Commission support for restaurant conversions in this corridor.
comparables.key_takeaway: Conversion from wine shop to full-service restaurant was approved three decades ago, establishing precedent for food service uses at closely spaced intervals along West Portal Avenue, a pattern that continues today.

comparables.why_comparable: A 2019 agency referral at 160 West Portal Ave (109 m away, NCD-WEST PORTAL) for a Limited Restaurant health permit approval, showing recent regulatory activity at the same address as Toast Eatery and confirming ongoing restaurant operations.
comparables.key_takeaway: Health Department referrals for restaurant uses are approved within a week in West Portal when the use is established or principally permitted, indicating streamlined agency coordination for compliant food service operations.

patterns.pattern: Restaurant uses on West Portal Avenue are consistently approved when principally permitted in NCD-WEST PORTAL. All use decisions and agency referrals for restaurants within 300 m approved the use, with only one imposing restrictive operating conditions.

The one conditioned restaurant approval in the last decade (Kaleifornia, 2019) imposed unusually restrictive hours (6 a.m. to 8 p.m.) plus standard eating-and-drinking conditions (trash, noise, odor, community liaison). Most other restaurant approvals show no extracted conditions, suggesting Kaleifornia faced site-specific concerns.

West Portal restaurants with evening hours (closing between 9 p.m. and 10:30 p.m.) have operated for decades without recorded enforcement issues. Fuji Restaurant has closed at 10:30 p.m. since 1999, and the neighborhood supports dining activity into the evening.

Standard eating-and-drinking conditions appear when the Commission imposes project-specific requirements: sidewalk maintenance within one-block radius, soundproofing, odor control, on-site trash storage, and appointment of a community liaison officer.

Agency referrals (Health Department, ABC) for continuation or ownership changes of existing restaurants are approved within days to weeks (7 to 30 days typical), while new-use CUAs requiring Planning Commission hearings take 4 to 5 months from filing to decision.

No denials of restaurant uses appear in the West Portal record over the last decade. The one record marked 'Closed - Disapproved' (MB1401288 at 160 West Portal) states in its description that it was 'Approved per Planning Commission Motion #19363', indicating a data artifact, not an actual denial.

Change-of-use approvals from non-food to food service are routine in West Portal when the new use is principally permitted: conversions from wine shop to restaurant (1991) and limited to full restaurant service (2015) both received CUA approval within 109 m of the subject site.

findings.text: Planning Code Section 729 principally permits restaurant use on the first story in the NCD-WEST PORTAL zoning district, and the 2012 site history shows Planning approved a restaurant with Type 41 ABC license at 243-255 West Portal Ave.
Planning Code Section 729 requires a Conditional Use Authorization for uses of 2,500 square feet or more in the NCD-WEST PORTAL district, and 3,995 square feet exceeds that threshold.
The description does not state whether the business is part of a chain, so whether formula retail conditional use applies under Section 729 is not established by the rules.

The description does not state what the space was last used as, and no active ABC license is on file, so whether a laundromat change-of-use conditional use (Planning Code Section 202.12, in effect 2021-12-20 to 2024-12-20) applies is not established.

Within 1,000 ft over the last 10 years, N=4 dated use decisions for comparable restaurant projects: 3 approved outright, 1 approved with conditions (a 2019 CUA at 36 West Portal Ave limited hours to 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily), zero denials.

Recent nearby approvals at 170 West Portal (2011 CUA for full-service restaurant Sweet Orchid, 109 m) and 160 West Portal (2015 CUA upgrading limited to full restaurant Toast Eatery, 109 m) were approved without extracted conditions, indicating routine approval when principally permitted.

approvals.summary: A Health Permit to Operate is required after plan check and pre-opening inspection; no discretionary hearing is needed, and recent health referrals for restaurants at nearby West Portal addresses were approved within 7 days.

findings.text: California Retail Food Code Sections 114380-114381 and San Francisco Health Code Article 8 require a health permit to operate any food facility; the permit is issued after plan check, final inspection and certification of a food safety manager, without a hearing.
The health permit application is referred to the Planning Department for zoning review under the Interagency Permit Referrals procedure.

Agency referrals for restaurant health permits at 160 West Portal Ave (filed 2019-08-28, decided 2019-09-04) and 118 West Portal Ave (filed 2020-09-28, decided 2020-10-27) were approved within 7 to 30 days in the NCD-WEST PORTAL district.

findings.text: The California Building Code classifies a restaurant or bar with 100 seats (at least 50 people) as Assembly Group A-2; a space for fewer than 50 people is Group B.
The existing occupancy group of the space is not in public records; only plans or an inspection show it, so whether a change of occupancy from Group B to Group A-2 occurs is not established.

The description states tenant improvements are planned and that the project merges two storefronts; kitchen build-out, hood installation, restrooms, ADA upgrades and storefront merger require a building permit with architect-stamped plans.
Building permit applications are referred to the Planning Department under Planning Code Section 175(a) for zoning review.

expected_conditions.condition: Hours of operation limited to specific daily times, potentially 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. or earlier if the Commission finds evening activity impacts nearby residential uses.
expected_conditions.basis: The one conditioned restaurant approval in the last decade (Kaleifornia, 36 West Portal Ave, 2019) imposed 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. hours. However, Fuji Restaurant at 301 West Portal Ave has operated until 10:30 p.m. since 1999 without extracted conditions, so the Commission's approach varies by site and proposal. The current concept's pre-midnight hours fall between these examples.

expected_conditions.condition: Sidewalk maintenance within a one-block radius: the operator shall monitor and keep the sidewalk free of litter associated with the business during business hours, per Police Code Article 1 Section 34.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard eating-and-drinking condition imposed on Kaleifornia (2019 CUA). This condition appears when the Commission approves food service uses requiring conditional use authorization.

expected_conditions.condition: Soundproofing requirement: the premises shall be adequately soundproofed so that incidental noise is not audible beyond the premises or in other sections of the building, and fixed-source equipment noise shall not exceed San Francisco Noise Control Ordinance limits.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard eating-and-drinking condition imposed on Kaleifornia (2019 CUA). This condition is typical for restaurant approvals in mixed-use districts with residential above or adjacent.

expected_conditions.condition: Odor control: appropriate equipment shall be installed and maintained to prevent significant noxious or offensive odors from escaping the premises.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard eating-and-drinking condition imposed on Kaleifornia (2019 CUA). Full-kitchen restaurants with 100 seats generate cooking odors, so the Commission routinely requires proper ventilation and odor control systems.

expected_conditions.condition: Garbage, recycling and compost containers shall be kept within the premises and hidden from public view, and placed outside only when being serviced by the disposal company, per Department of Public Works guidelines.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard eating-and-drinking condition imposed on Kaleifornia (2019 CUA). This condition addresses trash visibility and vermin control in high-pedestrian commercial corridors.

expected_conditions.condition: Appointment of a community liaison officer to address concerns of nearby property owners and occupants, with written notice of the liaison's contact information provided to the Zoning Administrator and registered neighborhood groups.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard eating-and-drinking condition imposed on Kaleifornia (2019 CUA). This condition facilitates ongoing communication between the operator and the neighborhood during and after construction.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain written confirmation from Planning Department whether the proposed 3,995 sq ft restaurant at 243 West Portal Ave requires a Conditional Use Authorization and whether the prior use at this address affects the pathway.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Request a pre-application meeting with Planning's Zoning Administrator or a planner assigned to the West Portal neighborhood. Bring the 2012 agency referral records (MB1200147 and MB1201143) showing prior restaurant approval at 243-255 West Portal Ave. Ask: (1) whether the 2,500+ sq ft size trigger applies to this specific site given the prior use, (2) what the records show as the last use of the space, and (3) whether the concept as described requires a CUA or can proceed with over-the-counter zoning review. If a CUA is required, ask for guidance on the pre-application community meeting and environmental review timeline.

filing_playbook.action: File for a Conditional Use Authorization with San Francisco Planning if Planning confirms one is required for the 3,995 sq ft size or other triggers.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the CUA application with site plans, floor plans showing the 100-seat layout, proposed hours of operation (state specific closing time, e.g., 10 p.m. daily), a narrative explaining the storefront merger and restaurant operations, a good-neighbor policy (trash, noise, odor management, community liaison contact), and photographs of the existing space. State that no alcohol service is proposed and that the use is principally permitted under Section 729. Address each Section 303 finding: the use serves neighborhood needs without adverse effects on adjacent uses, the operator will maintain the sidewalk and comply with noise and odor controls, and the hours align with existing West Portal restaurants (cite Fuji closing at 10:30 p.m. if relevant). Hold the required pre-application community meeting and submit the summary with the application. Budget 4-5 months from filing to Planning Co…

filing_playbook.action: Register the business entity with the California Secretary of State and obtain an Employer Identification Number (EIN) from the IRS.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File LLC Articles of Organization (Form LLC-1, $70) or Articles of Incorporation (Form ARTS-GS, $100) online at bizfile.sos.ca.gov. File the Statement of Information within 90 days ($20 for LLC, due every 2 years). Obtain the EIN immediately online at irs.gov (free, issued same day Monday-Friday). The EIN and entity name are required for the San Francisco business registration, bank account, and all subsequent permits.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain San Francisco Business Registration Certificate (BAN) and file a Fictitious Business Name statement if the restaurant name differs from the legal entity name.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register online at treasurer.sfgov.org with the EIN and entity documentation. The fee is tiered by gross receipts ($55-$700 plus $4 state fee for 2026-27). The Business Account Number (BAN) is required for all city permits. File the Fictitious Business Name (DBA) statement with the County Clerk in person or by mail ($60-$120), then publish once a week for four weeks in a court-approved newspaper and file proof of publication within 45 days. Banks and Planning will ask for the filed FBN statement.

filing_playbook.action: Submit Public Health plan check application for the new full-kitchen restaurant build-out to SF Department of Public Health Environmental Health Branch.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply online at sfdph.org with the BAN, two sets of scaled drawings showing kitchen layout, equipment specifications, finishes (walls, floors, ceilings), hand sinks, three-compartment sink, dishwasher, hood and suppression system, and the menu. State that this is a new restaurant merging two storefronts with a full commercial kitchen. The 2026-27 flat fee for a new restaurant plan review is $2,207 (8 hours of review time); extra review is billed at $276/hour. DPH will route the application to Planning for zoning review. Schedule a pre-final inspection at ~80% construction completion and a final inspection at least two weeks before the target opening date.

filing_playbook.action: Submit building permit application to SF Department of Building Inspection for tenant improvements, storefront merger, kitchen build-out, and any change of occupancy.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Hire a licensed architect to prepare plans for the storefront merger, kitchen, hood, restrooms, ADA upgrades, and egress for 100+ occupant load. The architect should confirm whether a change of occupancy from Group B to Group A-2 occurs and include a code analysis. Submit the permit application online at sf.gov/dbi with the architect's stamped plans, structural and MEP drawings, and the CUA approval (if required). Fees are a percentage of construction valuation ($800-$15,000 typical range). The application will be routed to Planning for zoning review under Section 175(a), to DPH for health plan check sign-off, to Fire for hood and egress review, and to PUC for grease interceptor requirements. Budget 14-120 days depending on plan completeness and whether corrections are needed.

filing_playbook.action: Install grease interceptor and submit Fats, Oils & Grease (FOG) Installation Verification Form to SF Public Utilities Commission.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The architect or plumber will size the grease-capturing device (interceptor or trap) based on SFPUC's FOG Control Ordinance. Install the device before the final DBI inspection. Submit the Installation Verification Form to SFPUC to qualify for a 14.2% sewer bill reduction. An undersized or missing interceptor will cause DBI to withhold final sign-off, so coordinate with the plumber and SFPUC inspector early.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain Fire Department Place of Assembly permit and commercial kitchen hood inspection for 100-seat restaurant.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: After the building permit is approved, file the Place of Assembly permit application at SFFD Permit Center, 49 South Van Ness Suite 560 ($446 base fee, 2026-27). Submit the floor plan showing occupant load calculation, exits, emergency lighting, and fire extinguishers. The hood suppression system plan review is routed with the building permit. Schedule the final fire inspection after MEP rough-in and before the DPH pre-opening inspection. The Fire Department will post an occupancy sign; this permit is required before the Health Permit to Operate can be issued.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain Certified Food Protection Manager certificate and California Food Handler Cards for all employees.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: One owner or employee must pass an ANSI-accredited food safety certification exam (ServSafe, Prometric, 360training) within 60 days of opening ($100-$250). All food-handling employees must obtain a California Food Handler Card within 30 days of hire ($7-$15, online course takes ~2 hours, valid 3 years). DPH inspectors will ask for the manager certificate at the pre-opening inspection and the list of food handler cards at all inspections.

filing_playbook.action: Apply for Health Permit to Operate at least one month before the target opening date.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply online at sfdph.org with the BAN, Location ID (LIN assigned during plan check), EIN, and the Certified Food Protection Manager certificate. The 2026-27 application fee is $470 (includes initial inspection); the annual license fee for restaurants and bars is $0 for 2026-28. DPH will schedule the pre-opening inspection after the final building and fire inspections are complete. The inspection confirms the facility matches the approved plans, all equipment is installed and operational, hand sinks have hot water, surfaces are sealed, and the manager certificate is on file. The permit is issued after the inspection passes; you cannot serve the public before it is issued.

timeline_cost.notes: The 120-300 day range and $5,200-$24,000 government cost range are the time and fees to obtain the approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (if required) and Health Permit to Operate. This is a time to approval, not a time to denial or withdrawal. The range assumes: (1) a CUA is required for the 3,995 sq ft size and takes 120-180 days from filing to Planning Commission hearing plus 30-day appeal period (typical CUA fee range $3,100-$15,000 depending on construction cost, with First Year Free waivers available for new storefront businesses); (2) health plan check takes 21-60 days ($828-$2,500, catalog:sf.health_plan_check) and the Health Permit to Operate takes 14-45 days ($470-$1,000, catalog:sf.health_permit) after construction is complete. If Planning confirms no CUA is required (e.g., the prior restaurant use at this address continues or the size trigger is waived), the timeline collapses to 35-105 days (health plan check plus permit to operate plus business registration) and government costs drop to $1,400-$3,700. Government costs shown exclude: building permit fees (a percentage of construction valuation, $800-$15,000 estimated, catalog:sf.building_permit), Fire Place of Assembly permit ($446-$1,500, catalog:sf.fire_place_of_assembly), sign permit ($300-$1,500, catalog:sf.sign_permit), state entity registration ($70-$150, catalog:ca.sos_entity_registration), business registration ($55-$700, catalog:sf.business_registration), FBN filing ($60-$120, catalog:sf.fictitious_business_name), food safety certifications ($107-$265 total, catalog:ca.food_safety_manager_cert and catalog:ca.food_handler_card for 20 employees), music licenses ($600-$5,000/year, catalog:us.ascap_license and catalog:us.bmi_license), and workers' compensation insurance premiums (percentage of payroll, not a government fee). Construction duration (storefront merger, kitchen build-out) is not included in this timeline; it runs in parallel with or after the CUA hearing and adds 2-6 months to the overall project schedule. The critical path item is confirming with Planning whether a CUA is required; that answer determines whether the timeline is 3-5 months (no CUA) or 6-10 months (CUA required).
